source_caption:
To authentically portray Vincent Vega’s lethargic, opiate-induced demeanor without actually partaking in illicit substances, John Travolta sought the advice of a friend who was a recovering heroin addict. The friend explained that the euphoric, heavy-limbed sensation of the drug could be approximated safely through a very specific physical method: drinking copious amounts of tequila while soaking in a hot tub. Travolta committed to this unconventional acting exercise alongside his wife, soaking in hotel baths until they achieved a simulated state of groggy, liquid relaxation. This visceral, sensory preparation allowed Travolta to organically capture Vincent’s distinctive, slow-rolling gait, heavy-lidded expressions, and delayed reactions, effectively bringing the character’s signature narcotic haze to the screen without relying on exaggerated caricatures of addiction.

Pulp Fiction (1994), directed by Quentin Tarantino, starring John Travolta, Uma Thurman, Samuel L. Jackson, Bruce Willis. The lives of two mob hitmen, an aging boxer, a gangster’s wife, and a pair of diner bandits intertwine in a highly stylized, non-linear narrative of violence and redemption unfolding across Los Angeles.

source_details.title: Pulp Fiction
source_details.synopsis: Pulp Fiction is a 1994 American crime film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino from a story he conceived with Roger Avary. It tells four intertwining tales of crime and violence in Los Angeles. The film stars John Travolta, Samuel L. Jackson, Bruce Willis, Tim Roth, Ving Rhames, and Uma Thurman. The title refers to the pulp magazines and hardboiled crime novels popular during the mid-twentieth century, known for their graphic violence and punchy dialogue. Tarantino wrote Pulp Fiction in 1992 and 1993, incorporating scenes that Avary originally wrote for True Romance (1993). Its plot occurs out of chronological order.
